items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I always was fond of Bud, you know.

ctx.x: Then another session with Mez Mezro and with Bud Freeman, and a little later in 1934, so there was . . .
What did I do with Bud Freeman? I don’t remember ever having played with Bud.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] No, that's what I might call an interesting anecdote, but I don't remember it.

ctx.x: Another thing, around that time. There's a -- in a discussion with Bud Freeman, that was not Bud Freeman, although he was involved -- it was Mezz Mezzrow, Mezzra -- Mezzra, in his book, 'Really the BLues' mentions that you helped him with what he calls the first interracial band; everybody's got the first interracial band -- he had it in 1933.
He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.
